description: Assess input handling, authorization and sessions only in deliberately vulnerable training apps. Guided explanations, six original visual diagrams, safe practice, trusted resource links, worked examples and a randomized quiz.

blocks.text: Lesson 6 — Web security testing with training applications

LEARNING OUTCOME
Assess input handling, authorization and sessions only in deliberately vulnerable training apps.

Safety rule: work only with devices, accounts and training applications you own or have explicit written permission to assess. Use synthetic information. A public system or a suspicious person is not permission.

Practice in OWASP Juice Shop or an authorized PortSwigger lab. Learn how requests, responses, cookies, tokens and APIs work. Keep the browser, proxy and target limited to that training environment. Do not test real company sites or accounts without written permission.

blocks.text: 2. Test the defense, not a person

Check whether the server validates data, verifies access for each record and protects session state. Use provided lab accounts and synthetic records. A successful login is not permission to read someone else’s information.

blocks.text: Use server-side authorization, parameterized database queries, context-aware output encoding, secure session settings and safe error handling. After a fix in your sample app, repeat the same lab check and show that the prohibited behavior is rejected.

blocks.text: Practice checklist: (1) read the lab rules, (2) use fabricated data or an isolated training target, (3) predict what the control should do, (4) test one small condition, (5) save only minimal evidence, and (6) explain the defensive follow-up. Stop and ask the owner if any target or action is outside the approved scope.

blocks.question: Before Lesson 6 testing, what should be confirmed?
options: A friend said it is okay
The exact target is covered by written permission
blocks.explanation: Written permission should define target and allowed methods.
blocks.hint: Use the lesson definitions and authorization boundary to reason through the options.

blocks.question: How should a finding from Lesson 6 be handled?
options: Save minimal redacted evidence and report through the approved channel
Include a real password as proof
blocks.explanation: Findings need scoped, protected and reproducible evidence.
blocks.hint: Use the lesson definitions and authorization boundary to reason through the options.

blocks.question: What requires the learner to stop?
options: Target is out of scope or testing may cause unexpected harm
A lab result needs an explanation
blocks.explanation: Stop if scope or safety limits may be crossed.
blocks.hint: Use the lesson definitions and authorization boundary to reason through the options.

blocks.question: What is a sound step after applying a fix?

blocks.explanation: Retesting verifies the correction and preserves a useful record.

blocks.question: What should happen when a target is outside scope?
